svg.title: Moments & fluid pressure
svg.desc: Moment: M = Fd, in Nm; d is perpendicular pivot-to-force-line distance. 20 N × 0.30 m = 6 Nm. Longer lever → less force for the same turning effect. Balance, levers & gears: Clockwise moments = anticlockwise moments. 30 N at 0.20 m balances 15 N at 0.40 m. Adjacent gears rotate oppositely. Larger driven gear turns more slowly with greater turning effect in an ideal system. Pressure on an area: Fluid = liquid or gas. Forces are normal to surfaces. p = F/A, Pa = N/m². Smaller area → greater p for same F. 1 cm² = 10⁻⁴ m². Pressure with depth: p = hρg for a liquid column; increases with depth and density. 2 m water at g = 9.8 → 19,600 Pa above surface pressure. Δp = Δhρg; add atmospheric p if total requested. Upthrust: Greater pressure on bottom than top gives upward resultant. Floating at rest: upthrust = weight. Compare average density including air spaces; hollow steel ships can float. Atmosphere: Air molecules collide with surfaces. Higher altitude has less air above, lower density and lower pressure. For submerged objects, compare weight/upthrust and include other forces if present; sinking does not mean zero upthrust.
